text:
Grace O'Connor: Dropping v3 of the regulated ABM email sequence copy for review (FinServ + Healthcare variants). Main asks: subject lines + CTA + compliance-safe wording.

Grace O'Connor: Email 1 (FinServ) draft:
Subject options:
1) "Private LLM inference in your VPC (audit-ready)"
2) "Reduce LLM latency + keep data in-region"
3) "Question on your LLM deployment constraints"

Body:
"Hi {{first}},
Teams in Financial Services are getting pressure to ship LLM features without expanding data exposure.
Redwood Inference helps you run open models with predictable latency and cost, with Hosted → Dedicated → Private deployments (VPC/on‑prem), audit logs, and KMS/HSM integration options.
Would it be crazy to do a 20‑min technical deep dive next week? If useful, we can also share our security FAQ + Private reference architecture." 

CTA options:
A) "Book a 20‑min VPC/private deployment deep dive"
B) "Reply with your security owner and I’ll loop in our CISO"

Grace O'Connor: Email 1 (Healthcare) draft is similar but references PHI + retention/residency.

Grace O'Connor: Biggest concern: are we saying anything that Security will hate? :grimacing:

Rohan Mehta: +1. Also the subject line "audit-ready" feels strong. Might trigger proof requests we can’t fulfill in first touch.

Ben Carter: From Growth POV: subject #3 has the best reply rate historically. But we need a hook that still signals we actually do Private.

Soojin Lee: PMM notes:
- Agree "audit-ready" is risky. Maybe "audit logging" instead of "audit-ready".
- "Keep data in-region" is ok *if* we don’t imply guaranteed residency everywhere. Maybe "data residency options".
- "KMS/HSM integration options" is good but we should avoid sounding like we support every HSM under the sun.

Soojin Lee: Suggest subject line set:
1) "Private LLM inference in your VPC"
2) "Audit logs + dedicated/private deployments for LLMs"
3) "How are you handling LLM data + security reviews?"

Grace O'Connor: Nice. Re: residency wording — should we say "region controls" or "residency options"?

Olga Petrov: GRC take: please avoid anything that reads like a certification claim.
- Don’t say “HIPAA compliant” or “PCI compliant” in outbound.
- Don’t say “meets FFIEC requirements” etc.
- “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA” is okay if we’re prepared to follow through.

Olga Petrov: For healthcare version, prefer: “supports PHI workloads with Private/VPC/on‑prem deployment options” vs “PHI-safe” or “HIPAA-ready.”

Dr. Aisha Rahman: +1 to Olga.
Also please remove “loop in our CISO” as a CTA. I can join security review calls but we shouldn’t imply CISO involvement for every prospect. Better: “loop in our Security/GRC team.”

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Wording edits:
- Replace “without expanding data exposure” with “while maintaining existing data handling controls.”
- Replace “audit logs” with “audit logging capabilities” (sounds less like a guarantee).
- If you mention retention, don’t claim “no retention” unless you specify deployment mode + configuration. We’ve seen prospects interpret that literally.

Marcus Lin: Security Eng nit: “KMS/HSM integration options” → “customer-managed keys (KMS) support; HSM integrations available on request” (so we’re not committing to specific vendor support in cold email).

Marcus Lin: Also, please don’t imply we “run in your VPC” for Hosted/Dedicated. Make sure Private/VPC is clearly scoped to the Private deployment option.

Grace O'Connor: Super helpful. Proposed updated Email 1 (FinServ):
Subject: "Private LLM inference in your VPC"
Body tweak:
“Teams in Financial Services are shipping LLM features while maintaining existing data handling controls.
Redwood Inference supports predictable latency/cost with Hosted → Dedicated → Private deployments. For regulated workloads, Private deployments can run in your VPC (or on‑prem) with audit logging capabilities and customer-managed keys (KMS).”
CTA: “Open to a 20‑min technical deep dive on Private/VPC deployment + security review flow?”

Grace O'Connor: Any red flags with “can run in your VPC”?

Marcus Lin: That’s fine as long as it’s explicitly “Private deployments can run…” (which you did).

Olga Petrov: Add one sentence to set expectations on security artifacts:
“SOC 2 Type II report and security FAQ are available under NDA.”

Ben Carter: Does “under NDA” reduce replies? We can phrase as “available under NDA if needed” so it’s not a blocker.

Soojin Lee: +1 “if needed.” Also recommend we don’t over-index on “Hosted → Dedicated → Private” jargon in first email. Maybe one line: “Start with hosted for evals; move to Dedicated/Private when security requires.”

Avery Johnson: AE POV: keep the ladder, it’s a differentiator. But make it skimmable. Maybe: “Evaluate quickly (Hosted), then move to Dedicated/Private for isolation + security.”

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Fine to mention the path, but avoid promising “fast security review.” You can say “we can share questionnaire-ready responses” or “we have a security FAQ addendum.”

Grace O'Connor: Got it. Updating copy to:
- “questionnaire-ready” instead of “fast/accelerated”
- “audit logging capabilities”
- “customer-managed keys (KMS); HSM integrations available on request”
- CTA: “20‑min technical deep dive”

Grace O'Connor: For Healthcare version, swapping “PHI-safe” → “supports PHI workloads” and removing “HIPAA-ready.”

Soojin Lee: One more CTA thought: include a low-friction option:
“Worth sending over the Private reference architecture + security FAQ addendum?” (Yes/No)
Those get replies.

Rohan Mehta: Love that. We can use that in Email 2 as a soft bump.

Grace O'Connor: Ok final proposed subject line list (for A/B):
A) Private LLM inference in your VPC
B) Audit logging + Private deployments for LLMs
C) How are you handling LLM security reviews?

Grace O'Connor: If no objections in next hour, I’ll lock and hand to Tyler for HubSpot build.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Approved with the changes above. Please send me the final text that goes into HubSpot so we’re not drifting from this thread.

Olga Petrov: +1. Also please make sure the word “compliant” doesn’t appear anywhere in the sequence.

Ben Carter: :thumbsup: Ship it. Send final for UTM + landing page alignment once it’s in HubSpot.

Grace O'Connor: Will do. Thanks all.
